outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Language Model Alignment and Preference Learning
outline.description: This chapter introduces the fundamental problem of aligning large language models (LLMs) with human intent. It explains why standard unsupervised training leads to unpredictable outputs and introduces Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) as the dominant solution. The chapter details the standard RLHF pipeline, highlighting its computational complexity and instability issues.
subtopics: The limitations of unsupervised pre-training for safety and controllability
Introduction to Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and instruction following
The concept of Relative Human Preferences
Standard RLHF Pipeline: Reward Modeling and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Challenges of RLHF: Sampling costs, instability, and complexity

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Mathematical Foundations of Policy Optimization
outline.description: This chapter provides the rigorous mathematical background necessary to understand the derivation of Direct Preference Optimization. It covers the formulation of constrained reinforcement learning objectives, the relationship between reward functions and optimal policies, and the theoretical properties of preference models.
subtopics: Formulating Alignment as Constrained KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
The Constrained MDP objective: Maximizing reward subject to KL-divergence constraints
Analytical Solution for Optimal Policy under Linear Reward
Equivalence Classes of Reward Functions and Under-specification in Bradley-Terry
Closed-form mapping from Reward to Policy ($\pi_r$)
Reparameterization: Expressing Rewards in terms of Polices
